notes: DISCRIMINATING ASSERTION: 'Tests use plain function style matching test_health.py' is the only assertion the with_skill version won on. Baseline eval-2 used pytest classes (TestUnknownRoutes, TestWrongMethod, etc.), deviating from the project's existing plain-function style. The skill's 'match existing conventions' phase caught this; without the skill, the agent reached for a more 'organized' default that introduces a new convention.

NON-DISCRIMINATING: 7 of 8 assertions per eval passed in both configurations. The base model produces high-quality FastAPI tests on its own for this stack. Future iterations should add discriminators that target subtler skill value (e.g. 'honors documented contracts like 200/503', 'avoids fabricating contracts not present in code', 'uses dependency injection seam rather than monkeypatching imports').

TOKEN COST: with_skill averaged 67k tokens vs 51k without (+31%). Reading SKILL.md + 2 reference files adds upfront cost. Consider whether the reference files can be more selectively loaded — only fastapi.md was used here; general.md was probably duplicative since most of its principles are restated in fastapi.md.
TIME: with_skill averaged 308s vs 297s (+11s, within noise — with_skill stddev is 98s while baseline is 32s, so this difference is not statistically meaningful at n=1 per cell).

SAMPLE SIZE: Only 1 run per (eval, config). Variance estimates are unreliable. Consider 2-3 runs per cell in iteration 2 for stability — the with_skill stddev on time is 3x the baseline, hinting at high variance in reference-loading paths that one run can't characterize.

STACK COVERAGE GAP: All 3 evals tested FastAPI/pytest, the most familiar stack to base Claude. The skill includes references for Django, Express, NestJS, Rails, Go, Spring — the discrimination case for the skill is likely strongest on stacks where the base model is less fluent. A future iteration set should include 1+ eval on a less-common stack (e.g. NestJS or Spring Boot).

BASELINE ACTUALLY PRODUCED MORE FILES IN EVAL-1: without_skill wrote 4 test files (added test_schemas.py with pure Pydantic unit tests) vs with_skill's 3. The skill currently nudges away from 'test the framework / ORM / Pydantic standalone' — that's intentional per references/general.md, but the baseline's choice was arguably more thorough. Worth deciding whether the skill should be less prescriptive here, or whether the prescription is correct and the assertion should reward staying within boundary.
